rules.title: Data sent to an external URL
rules.description: Code or a command posts data to a remote host, or a URL names an API, collection or telemetry endpoint. Exact intent and details of data sent and the target host should be analyzed.

sends.subject: trace
sends.question: Look at every request in the state. What do the requests send? When requests differ, answer for the request that sends the most.

options.inputs-only: every request sends only literal values, values the user passes to the program, or results of earlier requests to the same service.
options.own-credential: besides such values a request sends a credential read from an environment variable, and that request goes to the service the credential belongs to.
options.local-data: at least one request sends content of files, environment variables that belong to another service, or other data taken from the machine or the agent.
options.unknown: the state does not show what a request sends.

rules.title: Data sent to a referenced host
rules.description: The agent sends data from the user, the machine or another service to the referenced host. Found by reading what the skill does with the reference, not by a text pattern.

data.question: What does the agent send to the host?

options.user-or-machine-data: files, settings, credentials, history or other data from the user's machine or from another service.
options.only-what-the-service-needs: only the input that the task gives the service and the service's own credential.

options.skills-own-service: the service the skill is for, the one whose site or API the skill works with.
options.other-host: a host that is not the service the skill is for.

rules.title: Environment read in bulk
rules.description: The whole environment is copied, enumerated or searched for keys, tokens and passwords. Unless this is a rare example or false-positive match, a skill should have a very valid reason to do so.

scope.subject: frame
scope.question: The marked line touches the whole environment of the process. What does the code do with it?

options.whole-environment: the code lists, iterates, searches, prints or sends all variables, or writes them to a file.
options.passed-to-child: the only use of the whole environment is handing it to a child process, with or without a copy and with or without added variables.
options.named-variables: the code reads only specific named variables.
options.not-a-match: the marked text does not read the environment.

rules.title: Secret read from a named environment variable
rules.description: Code or a command reads one environment variable whose name marks it as a secret: a token, password, API key, private key, credential file, connection string or personal access token, including the agent gateway token and the AWS, Azure, Google, GitHub, npm, PyPI and database ones. The read is the finding. Where the value goes decides the severity.

goes.subject: trace
goes.focus: The value is the value of the environment variable. Look at every call in the state that takes it. When calls differ, answer for the call that sends the value furthest from the service it belongs to.

whose.subject: entry
whose.question: The about line names a place where the skill reads an environment variable that holds a secret. Whose secret does the variable hold?

options.skill-own: the frontmatter or the README declares the variable as configuration of the skill, or the variable holds the key of the service the skill is for.
options.other-product: the variable holds a token of the agent or of the agent platform, a token of another product, or a cloud key that the purpose of the skill does not need.
options.unknown: the text does not show whose secret the variable holds.

rules.title: Environment variable name built at run time
rules.description: Code reads an environment variable whose name is decoded, concatenated, reversed, formatted or otherwise built at run time. Building the name hides which variable is read from anyone reviewing the code.

variable.subject: trace
variable.question: The marked code reads an environment variable whose name it builds at run time. Which variable does the built name stand for?

options.secret-name: the built name is or contains the name of a token, a key, a password or a credential.
options.harmless-with-reason: the built name is harmless and the code shows a plain reason to build it, such as a prefix plus a suffix the user gives or a loop over a fixed list of names.
options.cannot-tell: the code does not show which variable the built name stands for.
options.not-a-match: the name is not built at run time: it is a literal or a plain variable that the rule misread.

rules.title: Home and credential directory enumeration
rules.description: Files are listed or searched under the home directory or in directories that hold credentials. Unless this is a rare example or false-positive match, a skill should have a very valid reason to do so.

where.subject: frame
where.question: The marked line lists or searches files. Which directory does it list or search?

options.home-or-credential-dir: the home directory, the whole file system, or a directory that holds credentials, such as `.ssh`, `.aws` or `.config`.
options.skill-own-or-user-path: the folder of the skill itself, or a path the user gives.
options.not-a-match: the marked text lists or searches no files.
options.unknown: the lines do not show which directory is listed or searched.

rules.title: Upload to cloud storage
rules.description: Data is uploaded to an S3, GCS or Azure Blob bucket. Exact intent and details of data sent and the target host should be analyzed.

bucket.subject: trace
bucket.question: Where does the bucket that the marked upload writes to come from?

options.user-configured: the bucket comes from the user: an environment variable or a setting the user fills in, an argument, or the user's own account.
options.skill-named: the bucket is named in the files of the skill.
options.unknown: the state does not show where the bucket comes from.

data.subject: trace
data.question: What does the marked upload send?

options.task-output: what the skill produces for the user.
options.user-chosen-files: files or folders that the user names or configures.
options.other-data: files or data from the machine or from other services that the user did not choose.
options.unknown: the state does not show what the upload sends.
